text:
eli: Quick question — we're triaging Opal-3B from upstream (https://huggingface.co/upstream/opal-3b). License snippet looks restrictive, pasted below. Can we: (a) run quantization experiments on Dedicated/private infra, (b) host it on Redwood Hosted API? @legal-ops @mona

eli: ```
LICENSE: Opal Non-Commercial v1.0
- "Commercial use prohibited"
- "No redistribution of derivative model weights"
- "Attribution required: include 'Opal-3B (Upstream AI) © 2025' in docs"
```

mona: If quantization produces new weight files, does that count as a derivative? Also curious if eval benchmarks we publish (with numbers) are ok.

ravi: +1 on quantization question — our Optimize tests create int8 checkpoints to validate perf. Would those be "redistribution" if we keep them internal?

legal-ops: Short answer: treat quantization as creating a derivative. Most licenses that ban "redistribution of derivative weights" will prohibit sharing those quantized files outside the org (including to customers).

legal-ops: Hosting nuance: "Commercial use prohibited" usually blocks offering the model as part of a paid service (i.e., Redwood Hosted API) unless you have an explicit commercial license. Free internal research/evaluation is often tolerated, but not guaranteed — check the exact license text.

legal-ops: For clarity:
- Internal evals/benchmarks: OK if purely internal and no paid access.
- Dedicated/Private deployments to customers: if customer pays or it's part of a paid product, this is commercial and not allowed without upstream permission.
- Quantized weights: considered derivative; can't redistribute or hand them to customers.

mona: So we can run the quant experiments on our staging cluster for internal perf numbers, but must not include results or artifacts in customer deliverables?

legal-ops: You can publish benchmark numbers (e.g., latency, throughput) derived from evaluations, but avoid publishing the quantized model files or packaging them. Also include a note in any public benchmark stating the upstream license and attribution.

devex: I'll add a lock to the model onboarding checklist: "Opal-3B — LICENSE: non-commercial; blocked for hosted/dedicated until commercial license obtained". Can someone paste the exact attribution text we should show in model_card?

legal-ops: Suggested attribution line to put in model_card and internal docs: "Opal-3B — Upstream AI. Licensed under Opal Non-Commercial v1.0. Commercial use and redistribution of derivative weights prohibited without permission from Upstream AI."

eli: Thanks. Who will reach out to upstream for a commercial/license exception? We should ask if they offer a paid distro or an enterprise addendum that permits hosting and redistribution for quantized derivatives.

ravi: I can draft an email but want legal to approve.

legal-ops: Please use this template (feel free to edit):
```
Subject: Commercial licensing inquiry — Opal-3B

Hi Upstream AI team,

We are evaluating Opal-3B and are interested in offering model inference to customers as part of a managed service. Your published license indicates non-commercial use only and prohibits redistribution of derivative weights. Would you consider a commercial/redistribution license or an enterprise addendum that permits hosting and distribution of quantized variants? If so, please share pricing/terms or next steps.

Thanks,
[Name], Redwood Inference
```

mona: Also — if upstream is ok with us hosting but forbids redistribution, could we still run Hosted API as a thin inference proxy (no weight distribution) if they permit commercial use? I.e., we never hand out weights, we just run them on our infra.

legal-ops: That would likely be allowed if they grant commercial hosting rights specifically. Key is the license grant: it must explicitly include "right to host/run service" or "commercial use". If permission is only for internal research, hosted paid service is not permitted.

eli: Action items: eli -> open upstream ticket + cc legal (ravi will draft), devex -> add model_card + onboarding blocker, mona -> run internal quant experiments but seal artifacts and tag as "do-not-distribute", legal-ops -> review outreach draft. :thumbsup:

ravi: I'll post a draft in #legal-drafts and link back here when ready.

legal-ops: FYI — if they respond asking for revenue share vs one-time fee, escalate to sales/partnerships.

eli: Cool. Keeping this thread as the record.
